thesis: Insmed rose about 14.1% to $170.18 (from $149.09) on 17.9x volume after Sanofi agreed to acquire it for $175 per share in cash, about $41.0B in total (Sanofi 6-K), a roughly 46% premium to the close before reports of the talks. Closing is expected in 1H 2027, subject to Insmed stockholder approval and regulatory clearances. The shares traded in a tight band just under the offer, so the remaining upside is a ~2.8% spread over several months, while a broken deal would expose them to the pre-report level. The strongest plausible positive, a competing bid, isn't ruled out, and this run found no closing-timeline detail beyond 1H 2027. The litigation check found no lawsuit or investigation over the deal and no restatement. Medium; avoid.
invalidation: A competing proposal above $175 emerges, or the merger agreement is terminated.
sources: Proactive Investors (stock jumps after Sanofi bid): https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1102371/insmed-stock-jumps-14-after-sanofi-s-41-billion-bid-1102371.html

thesis: BILL Holdings slipped about 0.3% to $61.45 (from $61.61) on 2.6x volume, pinned below the $63.25 per-share cash price in its Nov 19 agreement to be taken private by TPG with Corpay as minority partner (8-K), with closing expected in 1H 2027 subject to stockholder and other approvals. invalidation: A competing proposal above $63.25 emerges, or the merger agreement is terminated.

thesis: Kymera rose another 15.7% to $173.94 (from $150.37) on 4.8x volume, a day after a 30.4% gain on its Nov 23 BROADEN2 Phase 2b results (company release, 8-K): once-daily oral KT-621 met all primary and secondary endpoints in 244 atopic dermatitis patients, with a 45% placebo-adjusted mean EASI reduction and 40% placebo-adjusted EASI-75 at the mid dose, and a first Phase 3 planned by mid-2027; UBS raised its target to $205 and RBC, Guggenheim, Morgan Stanley and BTIG also raised. The same day it priced an upsized offering of 11,638,000 shares at $150.37 for about $1.75B, with a 30-day option on 1,745,700 more. The drug is not approved and hasn't been tested head-to-head against Dupixent. The litigation check found 2026 plaintiff-firm fiduciary-duty solicitations (Purcell & Lefkowitz, Kuehn Law) with no filed complaint or scheduled step, and no restatement. A strong confirmed readout paired with a completed $1.75B equity raise carries a dilution risk flag, which makes this low.
invalidation: Phase 3 design or FDA feedback undercuts the Phase 2b result, a safety signal emerges, or the shares close back below the $150.37 offering price.

thesis: BIP Inc. edged up about 0.7% to $45.535 (from $45.24) on 2.8x volume in its second session under the BIP symbol after the Nov 19 simplification combined Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Brookfield Infrastructure Corp into one corporation. The company's own materials pointed to possible additional index inclusion without promising it, and this run found no index announcement and no other company news. The 60-day move and volume reflect the exchange of units and shares into the new entity rather than a new operating result. The litigation check found the ICSID arbitration over Peru's Rutas de Lima toll road (Procedural Order No. 2 issued July 6, 2026; no hearing date found) and a New York discovery fight tied to Peruvian criminal proceedings, with no restatement. thesis: Amentum jumped about 20.0% to $24.77 (from $20.65) on 5.5x volume after its fiscal Q4 2026 release (8-K dated Nov 23): adjusted EPS of $0.71 beat the $0.66 estimate, backlog rose 2.4% to $48.3B despite about $1.5B of NASA-related contract adjustments, it authorized its first share buyback of up to $500M, and it issued fiscal 2027 guidance. Counter-cases: Q4 revenue fell 8% to $3.62B (the company cites an extra week in the prior-year quarter) and full-year revenue fell 4% on joint-venture transitions, divestitures and the government shutdown; a pre-earnings preview flagged a larger NASA insourcing headwind for fiscal 2027; and the shares remain about 35% below their 52-week high. The buyback and backlog growth support the read, but the revenue trend and the NASA headwind aren't resolved. The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement (only a contract-award protest resolved in fiscal 2025). Medium.
invalidation: Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is cut, NASA insourcing widens, or the shares close back below the pre-report level (~$20.65).
sources: Yahoo Finance (stock up on beat and FY27 guidance): https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/amentum-amtm-stock-14-5-150051315.html

thesis: Abercrombie & Fitch jumped about 19.8% to $168.26 (from $140.45) on 4.5x volume, a new 52-week high, after its fiscal Q3 2026 release on Nov 24 (8-K): record net sales of about $1.44B, up 11% with comparable sales up 6% (its 16th straight quarter of growth), EPS of $3.82 vs about $3.09 expected, an operating margin of 15.5% vs a 13-14% outlook, and full-year guidance raised (sales growth about 6% from about 5%, EPS $13.70-13.90 from $13.10-13.60). About $20M of IEEPA tariff refunds helped the quarter; even without them the margin would still sit near the top of the outlook. The governance check found that former CEO Mike Jeffries was indicted in October 2024 on sex-trafficking charges and found fit to stand trial in August 2026, and the company is a co-defendant in a related civil suit alleging it knew of the abuse; no restatement. A confirmed beat and raise carries a governance-history risk flag from the former CEO's indictment, which makes this low.
invalidation: Comparable sales slow sharply in the holiday quarter, the raised guidance is cut, or the litigation tied to the former CEO produces a material company liability.
sources: StockTitan (record Q3 sales, 16th straight quarter of growth): https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ANF/abercrombie-fitch-co-reports-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-2dii8udhgn0h.html

thesis: Kohl's jumped about 19.6% to $25.345 (from $21.20) on 3.0x volume, about 1% below its 52-week high, after its fiscal Q3 2026 release on Nov 24 (8-K): comparable sales rose 1.2%, its first positive quarter in a stretch of declines, gross margin expanded 145bp, and full-year guidance was raised to comparable sales of flat to up 0.5%, operating margin of 4.7-4.9% and EPS of $4.30-4.50. Counter-case: GAAP EPS of $2.15 includes a $137M tax benefit, a $61M real-estate gain and about $45M of tariff refunds, and the coverage this run found doesn't reconcile those items cleanly with the $1.76 adjusted EPS it cites, so how much of the beat is operating can't be pinned down; a 1.2% comp is also modest for a department store. The margin expansion and positive comp are operating results, but the earnings-quality question stays open. The litigation check found no 2026 lawsuit, investigation or restatement; CEO Michael Bender has held the role permanently since November 2025, after the May 2025 for-cause firing of his predecessor over undisclosed vendor conflicts. Medium.
invalidation: Holiday-quarter comps turn negative again, the raised guidance is cut, or the shares close back below the pre-report level (~$21.20).

thesis: Dollar Tree jumped about 11.2% to $154.66 (from $139.10) on 2.8x volume, near its 52-week high of $156.89, after its fiscal Q3 2026 release on Nov 24 (8-K): adjusted EPS of $1.16 beat the ~$0.91 consensus, revenue rose 6.9% to $5.1B, and comparable sales rose 4.6%, above the 3-4% guide. Offsetting that, operating income fell about 10% and operating margin fell 110bp to 6.1% on tariff reinvestments, about $0.65 of the raised full-year adjusted EPS guide of $8.05-8.25 comes from tariff refunds, fourth-quarter guidance reportedly fell short of estimates, and management gave no 2027 guidance. A beat with a raise that rests largely on refunds, plus margin compression and a soft Q4 guide, makes the evidence mixed. The litigation check found a 2026 New York Attorney General settlement of about $559K over recalled applesauce pouches (resolved) and a January 2026 wrongful-death suit with no scheduled step found; no restatement. Low.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the guide, tariff-related margin pressure deepens, or the shares close back below the pre-report level (~$139).
sources: Startup Fortune (Q3 beat, refunds in the raise): https://startupfortune.com/dollar-tree-stock-jumps-after-q3-beat-and-a-raised-2026-profit-outlook/

thesis: Nutanix fell about 5.1% to $54.61 (from $57.56) in the regular session and traded near $50.20 after hours following its fiscal Q1 2027 release on Nov 24: revenue rose 15% to $772.4M vs about $762M expected, adjusted EPS of $0.73 beat $0.61, and ARR rose 15% to $2.63B; but full-year revenue guidance of $3.180-3.230B came in below expectations, and the company announced CEO Rajiv Ramaswami will step down once a successor is named. A below-consensus full-year guide plus an unplanned CEO search outweighs the quarter's beat; the strongest positive, the beat and ARR growth, doesn't resolve the guide. The litigation check found late-2025 and January 2026 plaintiff-firm investigations over the fiscal Q1 2026 guidance cut, with no filed complaint found, and no restatement. Medium; avoid.
invalidation: A strong new CEO is named and the next quarter beats with guidance raised back above consensus.

thesis: Best Buy rose about 2.7% to $99.59 (from $97.00) on 2.3x volume after its fiscal Q3 2027 release on Nov 24 (8-K), the first under CEO Jason Bonfig: enterprise comparable sales rose 6.1%, the highest in five years, vs about 2.3% expected (domestic online up 10.8%), adjusted EPS of $1.62 beat $1.49, revenue of $10.24B beat $9.90B, and full-year guidance was raised to comparable sales of 3.4-4.0% (from 1.9-3.0%) and adjusted EPS of $6.90-7.05 (from $6.70-6.90). Counter-case: the Q4 comparable-sales guide of 2-4% implies a sharp deceleration from Q3's 6.1%, and the shares are already up about 45% this year; the guide raise supports the read, but the deceleration isn't explained in the sources this run found. The CEO change was a planned succession announced in April. The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. Medium.
invalidation: Holiday-quarter comps land below the 2-4% guide, the raised guidance is cut, or the shares close back below the pre-report level (~$97).
sources: CNBC (comparable sales up 6.1%, highest in five years): https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/24/best-buy-bby-q3-2027-earnings.html

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22 on the Oct 21 proposal; a third sold at the +8% take-profit tier this morning). ROIV rose about 6.8% to $42.34 (from $39.63), touching a new 52-week high of $42.69; this run found no company disclosure dated after the Nov 9 fiscal Q2 release. That release reported $31.0M of LISRAYA (brepocitinib) net product revenue in its first five weeks after the Aug 27 FDA approval in dermatomyositis and a planned 1H calendar 2027 sNDA in non-infectious uveitis; an Investor Day is set for Dec 9. The counter-case named in the prior thesis stays open: the uveitis data are not an approval, the sNDA is months away, and the batoclimab Phase 3 miss shows pipeline risk. The litigation check found Moderna's pending Federal Circuit appeal of the government-contractor defense (it decides up to $1.3B more under the March settlement) with no ruling date found, and no restatement. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or the Federal Circuit rules for Moderna and removes the contingent payment.
